 www.hpca.gov. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding
 any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
 made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
 Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
 p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

 Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
 auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
 modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
 person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
 Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements
 to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

 PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC
 EQUIPMENT WHILE COUNCIL IS IN SESSION. Thank you.

PLEASE NOTE-The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  July 14, 2026  Page 1 of 6
  are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
 the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code, commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

 We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
 for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed sessions, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries should be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

6204 S Alameda St, Huntington Park, CA; Mayor Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Flores, Vice Mayor Sanabria, and Mayor
Martinez

ABSENT: Council Member(s): None

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Eduardo Sarmiento City Clerk; Cosme Lozano Chief of Police;
Cynthia Norzagaray Parks and Recreation Director; Andrew Sarega City Attorney; Karina

  DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

City Manager: Provided brief report on the highly anticipated Track Nights. Programs will
be transitioned fully to the parks department.

City Attorney: No Report.

City Clerk: Statement: After four-and-a-half years of dedicated service I have made the
difficult decision to pursue a new professional development opportunity. Serving the
residents of Huntington Park and supporting the City Council, City Administration, and the
democratic process has been one of the greatest privileges of my career. During my
tenure I have had the honor of collaborating with an exceptional team of professionals
whose commitment to public service has inspired me every day. I am sincerely grateful for
the trust, support and collaboration extended to me by City Staff, department directors,
and elected officials. The professional relationships I have developed throughout these
years are ones that I will always value and appreciate. I am proud of what we have
accomplished together and confident that City will continue to thrive through the
dedication and hard work of its employees. I remain committed to ensuring a smooth and
seamless transition and have been here to assist in that transition. With my final day
being this Thursday, July 16th, I want to thank the staff, administration, directors, and city
council for the opportunity to serve the City of Huntington Park, the community and its
residents. It has truly been an honor to contribute to the cities mission and be a part of this
organization that is dedicated to public service and leave immense gratitude and respect
to everyone that has been part of this journey.

Communication: City Hall services have been moved to the modular base behind the old
court building in the parking lot out behind of City Hall. Monday-Thursday 7am-5:30pm. Lt.
Silveranos has asked about a fireworks forum. It is Thursday, July 16th from 6-7:30pm and
will take place at Raul Perez Park. We will also have a Coffee with a Cop event on July
21st @Guajillo’s restaurant from 6pm-8pm. We invite the public. We also have National
Night at Freedom Park on Tuesday, August 4th from 5pm-8pm. All this information is
posted on social media. Candidate nominations are open until August 7th @5pm. Please
call to make an appointment if interested. Lastly, we will begin the surveys for the
broadband service.

Parks and Recreation: Wanted to thank everyone including staff, council, and community
that participated in the 4th of July event last week. We will also begin our summer night
event series on Friday, August 7th. And wanted to wish the absolute best on his future
endeavors. His professionalism and mannerism is unparalleled.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Martiz: Thank you to Eddie for your service. The City of Huntington
Park is very lucky to have you as the City Clerk. Especially in the last year for
implementing the By-district process and helping protect the democratic process. Making
sure we were moving the city to a better place. Please don’t forget about us and will be
cheerleading you wherever you go. Also, want to give a shoutout to Jeff and the finance
team that we finally implemented this finance system. These types of investments our
community members don’t really see, but hopefully they feel when they come with the
City. Congratulations to finance and Congratulations to the city.
 Councilmember Macias: Wishing everybody a good night. Mr. Sarmiento it has been
an honor having you here in the City. It was an honor of being part of the council that
was in the initial interview. I know you will be in an amazing rendition wherever you go.
Congratulations on your continued journey on your career. Your professionalism is part
of and wanted to thank you for showing your commitment to the community. It has been
a great honor and I’m sorry to see you go, it’s a great loss for us here in Huntington Park
and I know you will be a great gain to another community. Please always consider
Huntington Park your home.

Councilmember Flores: Wants to take time to recognize the amazing work you have
done here Eddie. With the City. The city has gone through a few transitions. The one
thing I can say about you if your professionalism, your love for the community is
something I admire. I once joked that you should run for office, I genuinely think that one
day you should step into that role one day. The City is going to have a good addition.

Vice Mayor Sanabria: Thank you everyone for all that you do. Thank you to the police
department for assisting with the fireworks control. Parks and Recreation amazing show,
wish it was a little longer. City Manager thanks for letting everyone know what is
occurring. Your professionalism is very impressive, and it is very hard to see you go. As
opportunities are granted to folks we can’t let them pass. I wish you nothing but the best.
I know you will continue to succeed and serve larger and larger communities.

Mayor Martinez: Thank you staff for having an amazing 4th of July event. City Clerk, you
were an amazing city clerk. It was a pleasure to get to know you. You were very
professional and I wish you success in life in your next chapter. You did a very good job.
Regarding upcoming elections, in my experience what occurred with the FBI and DA
investigation there were a lot of things done wrong behind our backs. I worry that the
same group will try to take control of the city and put pressure on directors and the city
managers to do stuff behinds out backs. I want to see how the city can have better
protection and let the public and council know if stuff is being done wrong. I would like to
have reform and ensure that we never have incidents like that never happen again.

  CLOSED SESSION

  None

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  None

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION: Mayor Martinez adjourned the meeting at 6:04pm. The next regular city council
meeting is set to be held on Tuesday, July 28th, 2026 @6pm at Raul Perez Park.

Respectfully submitted,

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
